input.title: Input Data
input.description: Start by saying what kind of data you have. Each platform reader is handed one folder — the top of the platform's output — and works out for itself which files inside it to read.

format.title: Data Type
format.description: The platform that produced the data. This choice decides what you are asked to select below and which reader the workflow runs. Whatever the platform, the result is the same: coordinates, feature groups and an optional background image, published as a Samui sample folder alongside a copy of the viewer.

sample_name.title: Sample Name
sample_name.description: Name of the published sample folder and the sample label shown in the browser. Letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores only.

folder.title: Xenium Output Folder
folder.description: The folder holding experiment.xenium — the top of the Xenium output. The reader takes cell centroids from cells.parquet (or cells.csv.gz), expression from the cell-feature matrix, any Xenium Ranger clustering under analysis/, and the morphology_focus image. Pixel size comes from experiment.xenium. Xenium Ranger v2.0+ writes morphology_focus as a multi-file directory, which this reader does not handle — those runs are published without a background image.

folder.title: Visium Output Folder
folder.description: The folder holding spatial/ — normally the Space Ranger outs/ directory, though the run directory wrapping it also works. The reader takes in-tissue spot positions, the filtered feature-barcode matrix, and any clustering under analysis/. Spot size is fixed at 55 microns and the scale is derived from spot_diameter_fullres. Space Ranger publishes only downsampled preview images, so Visium samples get no background image.

folder.title: Visium HD Output Folder
folder.description: The folder holding binned_outputs/ — the Space Ranger outs/ directory. The coarsest bin available is used (16 micron, else 8, else 2) so the browser stays responsive; select the outs/ folder itself rather than an individual bin. Per-cell segmented_outputs/ are not read.

folder.title: Platform Output Folder
folder.description: The top of the platform output, whichever platform produced it. Detection recognizes Xenium, Visium and Visium HD, and a Space Ranger run which only wraps an outs/ folder is followed into it. The run fails with a clear message if nothing matches — in that case pick the platform explicitly above. Auto-detect cannot reach SpatialData stores or individual files.

zarr.title: SpatialData Store
zarr.description: A SpatialData store, either a zipped .zarr.zip file or an unzipped .zarr directory. The first table in the store is exported: coordinates from its obsm['spatial'] or, failing that, from the centroids of the matching shapes element; expression from X; categorical obs columns as annotations. Images held in the store are not exported yet. Stores written by older versions of spatialdata may carry obs or var names that current versions reject (characters such as micron signs or slashes); these are sanitized on read, so those characters appear as underscores in the feature and annotation labels.

cells.title: Cell / Spot Table (required)
cells.description: One row per observation. Needs an ID column (id, cell_id, barcode, cell, obs or observation_id — otherwise the row number is used) and x / y coordinates (aliases such as x_centroid, center_x and pxl_col_in_fullres are accepted). Every remaining column becomes an overlay: text columns are grouped as Annotations, numeric columns as Cell metrics. Coordinates are assumed to be in image pixels unless you set Meters per pixel below.

matrix.title: Expression Matrix (required)
matrix.description: Counts, observations by features. For CSV or Parquet the first column holds the observation IDs and the rest are features; a transposed matrix is fine because the orientation is worked out by matching IDs against the cell table. A 10X .h5 file is read directly. Features named NegPrb*, NegControl*, SystemControl* or Blank-* are dropped as controls.

features.title: Feature Table (optional)
features.description: One row per feature, with the feature ID in the first column. If any column name contains "type" (as 10X feature_types does), only features typed Gene Expression are kept. Leave empty to use every feature in the matrix.

image.title: Background Image (optional)
image.description: TIFF or OME-TIFF drawn underneath the points. It must share the coordinate frame of the x / y columns in the cell table.

calibration.title: Calibration
calibration.description: Every reader derives these from the platform's own metadata. Set them only to override that — for example when the metadata file is missing, or for individual-file input, where coordinates are assumed to already be in image pixels. Leave blank to use the platform default.

pixel_size.title: Pixel Size (microns per pixel)
pixel_size.description: Microns per pixel of the platform image, used to convert micron coordinates into pixels. Overrides the value read from platform metadata — for Xenium that is pixel_size in experiment.xenium, which falls back to 0.2125 when the file is absent.

mpp.title: Meters per Pixel
mpp.description: Scale applied to both the coordinates and the background image, in meters per pixel. Overrides whatever the reader derived. Individual-file input defaults to 1.0, meaning coordinates are treated as raw image pixels.

spot_size.title: Marker Diameter (meters)
spot_size.description: Diameter of the marker drawn for each observation, in meters. Defaults to the physical size of the platform's unit: 55e-6 for a Visium spot, the bin width for Visium HD, 10e-6 for a Xenium cell, 1e-5 for a SpatialData store or individual-file input.

display.title: Display Options
display.description: How the published sample presents itself when it is opened in the browser.

coords_name.title: Name for the Observations
coords_name.description: Label used for the set of points, for example cells, spots, bins or beads. Defaults to whichever term suits the platform.

default_feature.title: Feature Shown on Load
default_feature.description: Name of the feature — usually a gene — displayed automatically when the sample opens. It must match a feature present in the data; anything else is ignored.

no_image.title: Skip the Background Image
no_image.description: Publish coordinates and features only. Useful when the Xenium morphology image is very large, fails to decode, or simply is not wanted. The other formats attach no background image in the first place (Visium and Visium HD ship only downsampled previews, and SpatialData images are not exported yet), so this has no effect on them.

convert_8bit.title: Downcast the Image to 8-bit
convert_8bit.description: Convert the background image to 8-bit before tiling. Produces a much smaller output and a faster first load, at the cost of dynamic range in dim regions.
